pregame.pressurePoint: Bears run game vs Falcons run defense. The Falcons are No. 3 of 32 against the run (33%) and No. 1 by EPA a carry (-0.25). The Bears rank No. 12 in rush success rate (44%) and No. 10 in EPA a carry (-0.02). A real edge, not a lock. The Bears will find the run hard going. Expect more second-and-long than usual. Watch Bears yards per carry through the first quarter. Under 3 and the game plan has to change.

edges.why: The Bears are No. 1 of 32 on passing downs (26%). The Falcons rank No. 31 in passing-downs success (27%). This is not a lean. It is a mismatch, and a prominent one. The Bears get off the field on long downs. Early-down efficiency is everything for the Falcons.

The Falcons are No. 2 of 32 in rush success rate (53%) and No. 2 in EPA a carry (0.13). The Bears rank No. 25 against the run (45%) and No. 29 by EPA a carry (0.04). This is not a lean. It is a mismatch, and a prominent one. Expect the Falcons to lean on the run early and often, and to keep leaning. Once the Bears load the box, play-action is the second punch.

The Falcons are No. 15 of 32 in pass explosiveness (1.34) and No. 19 in pass success rate (45%). The Bears rank No. 30 at limiting explosive passes (1.44) and No. 2 in pass success allowed (39%). A clear edge, the kind that shapes a game plan. The Falcons have the deep ball available. Watch whether the Bears roll a safety over after the first one.
